problem_text: If R is Noetherian and M and N are finitely generated R-modules, show that Ass Hom_R(M,N) = Supp M ∩ Ass N, where Supp M is the set of all primes containing the annihilator of M. Formal Lean target: associatedPrimes R (M →ₗ[R] N) = {p | p ∈ associatedPrimes R N ∧ Module.annihilator R M ≤ p}.
solution_text: The Lean file contains a `sorry` proof placeholder. Reconstructed mathematical proof: prove membership equivalence for each prime p. Use localization of associated primes and the finite-source Hom-localization isomorphism to identify (Hom_R(M,N))_p with Hom_{R_p}(M_p,N_p). Thus the global statement reduces to the local-ring lemma: for a Noetherian local ring (A,m) and finite A-modules P,Q, m ∈ Ass_A Hom_A(P,Q) iff P ≠ 0 and m ∈ Ass_A Q. For the forward direction, if a nonzero f : P → Q is killed by m, choose x with f(x) ≠ 0; then every a ∈ m kills f(x), so m ∈ Ass Q and P ≠ 0. For the reverse direction, m ∈ Ass Q gives an injection k=A/m ↪ Q. Since P is finite and nonzero over the local ring, Nakayama gives P/mP ≠ 0; choose a nonzero k-linear functional P/mP → k, lift it to a nonzero A-linear map P → k, and compose with k ↪ Q. This gives a nonzero element of Hom(P,Q) killed by m. Returning from localization, p ∈ Ass Hom_R(M,N) iff p ∈ Ass N and M_p ≠ 0; finite generation gives M_p ≠ 0 iff ann_R(M) ≤ p, yielding the formal target.
solution_summary: Reduce the associated-prime equality to a local ring lemma via localization and Hom-localization; prove the local lemma using m-torsion in Hom and a residue-field map P → P/mP → k ↪ Q; translate M_p ≠ 0 back to ann(M) ≤ p.
answer: associatedPrimes R (M →ₗ[R] N) = {p | p ∈ associatedPrimes R N ∧ Module.annihilator R M ≤ p}
structure_features: Set equality characterizing associated primes of Hom_R(M,N). The right side is an intersection of Ass N with Supp M, expressed formally as annihilator containment. The finite generation and Noetherian hypotheses signal a global-to-local proof using associated-prime localization, Hom-localization, and support equals V(annihilator).

key_insight: Do not try to globally construct a homomorphism whose annihilator is exactly p; localize at p, where the task becomes constructing a nonzero map killed by the maximal ideal, obtained from P → P/mP → k ↪ Q.

expected_ai_method: A bare AI may try to chase annihilators of individual nonzero homomorphisms M → N directly, or attempt a naive elementwise inclusion between Ass Hom and Ass N without changing to a local problem.
correct_method: Use set extensionality and localize at each prime p. Convert the problem to the local lemma m ∈ Ass Hom_A(P,Q) iff P ≠ 0 and m ∈ Ass Q, prove it with m-torsion and residue-field maps, then translate P≠0 back to ann(M)≤p via finite support.

rounds.question: First observe the problem structure only: what are the objects on the two sides of the equality, and what pointwise prime-ideal equivalence should be proved?
rounds.expected_answer: This is a set equality. The left side is the associated primes of Hom_R(M,N), and the right side is the associated primes of N that also contain ann(M), i.e. Supp M ∩ Ass N. For an arbitrary prime p, prove p ∈ Ass Hom iff p ∈ Ass N and M is nonzero at p.

rounds.question: List the standard tools for proving an associated-prime identity involving Hom of finite modules, without choosing a route yet.
rounds.expected_answer: Use associated primes via annihilators or R/p submodules, localization of associated primes, Hom-localization for finite source modules, support of finite modules as V(ann), local rings, residue fields, and Nakayama.

rounds.question: Try the direct route: start with a nonzero homomorphism f : M → N and track ann(f). How far does that get?
rounds.expected_answer: It helps relate the image of f to N in one direction, but the reverse direction requires constructing a global homomorphism with annihilator exactly p from p∈Ass N and ann(M)≤p. That is unnatural, so direct element tracking is not the right main route.

rounds.question: Localize at a fixed prime p: state the two localization facts needed and the resulting local-ring lemma.
rounds.expected_answer: Use p∈Ass_R X iff pR_p∈Ass_{R_p} X_p, and (Hom_R(M,N))_p ≃ Hom_{R_p}(M_p,N_p). The local lemma is: in a local ring (A,m), m∈Ass Hom_A(P,Q) iff P≠0 and m∈Ass Q.

rounds.question: Prove the forward direction of the local lemma: if m is associated to Hom_A(P,Q), what follows?
rounds.expected_answer: There is a nonzero f:P→Q killed by m. Pick x with f(x)≠0. For a∈m, a f(x)=(a f)(x)=0, so Q has a nonzero element killed by m; hence m∈Ass Q, and f≠0 also implies P≠0.

rounds.question: For the reverse direction, use the residue field: from P≠0 and m∈Ass Q, construct a nonzero P→Q killed by m.
rounds.expected_answer: m∈Ass Q gives an injection k=A/m↪Q. Since P is finite and nonzero over a local ring, Nakayama gives P/mP≠0. Choose a nonzero k-linear functional P/mP→k and compose P→P/mP→k↪Q. The resulting map is nonzero and killed by m.

rounds.question: Now return from the local lemma to the original formal set equality.
rounds.expected_answer: For every p, the local lemma gives p∈Ass Hom_R(M,N) iff M_p≠0 and p∈Ass_R N. Since M is finite, M_p≠0 iff p∈Supp M iff ann_R(M)≤p. Therefore Ass Hom_R(M,N) = {p | p∈Ass N ∧ ann M≤p}.
